name: Luo Aiping
current_role: Chairman and President, Guangdong Fangyuan New Materials Group (formerly Guangdong Fangyuan Environment; SSE STAR: 688148)
profile: Luo Aiping (罗爱平) founded Fangyuan in Jiangmen, Guangdong in 2002. The company makes lithium-battery cathode precursors (NCA/NCM) plus nickel-battery materials and lithium salts, and was a major NCA precursor supplier to Panasonic. He holds roughly 19.8% of the listed company. He studied at Central South University.
interesting_fact: Fangyuan began bulk-supplying high-nickel NCA precursors to Panasonic in late 2017. In 2021, NCA precursors brought in 1.326bn yuan, about 64% of revenue.
deep_cut_fact: He completed his undergraduate (1987), master's (1989) and doctoral (1998) degrees at Central South University. Fangyuan later commercialised a lithium-extraction process it co-developed with that university.
notes: Energy-relevant: battery materials. In Feb 2025 the company set up Guangdong Fangyuan Xincai to make high-purity electronic chemicals for chipmaking. The lithium-process detail is from the company homepage. Co-listed Wu Fang is a director and VP of the company.

name: Zheng Heping
current_role: Chairman, Delisi Group Co., Ltd. (Zhucheng, Shandong); Chairman, Zhucheng Tongluren Investment; Vice President, China Meat Association (per MarketScreener)
profile: Zheng Heping (郑和平) has chaired Delisi Group, a meat processor in Zhucheng, Shandong founded in 1986, since 1994. He chaired its listed arm, Shandong Delisi Food (SZSE: 002330), until March 2015. The group covers pig slaughtering, processed and canned meat, and prepared foods. MarketScreener lists his age as 75.
interesting_fact: Besides running Delisi, he is listed as a vice president of the China Meat Association, the national industry body for the meat sector.
notes: Roles come only from an aggregator (MarketScreener); not verified against primary filings. Baidu Baike was blocked. The listed company Shandong Delisi Food is now chaired by another Zheng family member (Zheng Qiankun per MarketScreener) and takes investor questions via ir.p5w.net. Hurun listings stopped in 2017. 'Alive' is unverified.

name: Yao Mingfang
profile: Hurun China (2015-2020) lists Yao Mingfang (姚明芳) as the wealth source behind 'Mingfang Steel'. The likely company is Wu'an Mingfang Iron and Steel in Handan, Hebei. It stopped production at its old plant on 13 July 2021 and was merged with Dongshan, Guangyao and other mills into Hebei Taihang Iron & Steel, which moved to the Nanminghe Industrial Park. No source read links Yao by name.
notes: Identity not confirmed: no English or Chinese web source read names Yao Mingfang as owner or chairman of Mingfang Steel. GEM lists Hebei Taihang Iron and Steel Group as the 100% parent. Company facts: https://kallanish.com/en/news/steel/market-reports/article-details/mingfang-steel-shuts-down-old-factory-for-relocation-0721 and https://gem.wiki/Wu_an_Mingfang_Iron_and_Steel_Co_Ltd. A Chinese company-registry lookup would settle it.

name: Pan Dongxiao
current_role: Chairman and General Manager, Zhongfu Information Inc. (中孚信息, SZSE ChiNext: 300659), Jinan
profile: Wei Dongxiao (魏东晓) has chaired and run Zhongfu Information, a Jinan-based cybersecurity and data-security firm, since 2013. Founded in 2002 and listed on ChiNext in 2017, Zhongfu sells classified-information protection, data-security and electromagnetic-security products, mainly to government bodies and state enterprises. Simply Wall St puts his direct stake at about 22%.
interesting_fact: Zhongfu says it launched China's first practical security/secrecy-inspection tool in 2004. In 2019 it won what it describes as China's largest Xinchuang (domestic IT substitution) security project.
deep_cut_fact: Zhongfu says that in 2018, at the 2nd National Secrecy Exhibition, it first proposed the concepts of 'smart secrecy' and 'digital government secrecy governance'. Its motto, 至诚于中 业成于孚, plays on the company name.
notes: The romanised name in the input ('Pan Dongxiao') does not match the Chinese name 魏东晓, which is Wei Dongxiao. That is the Zhongfu chairman (MarketScreener: 'Dong Xiao Wei', age 57). Address him as Wei Dongxiao. Company IR phone: 0531-66590077. Data-security angle may suit the data-center theme.

name: Jiang Shenghua
current_role: Founder, Chairman and General Manager, Zhejiang Huasheng Technology Co., Ltd. (SSE: 605180), Haining
profile: Jiang Shenghua (蒋生华), born 1962 per Yahoo Finance, founded Zhejiang Huasheng Technology in 1996 in Haining's warp-knitting industrial park. The company makes plastic composite materials: drop-stitch airtight fabric for paddle boards, gym mats and inflatable boats, plus tarpaulin and lightbox advertising fabric. It listed in Shanghai on 30 April 2021. He holds about 16% directly.
interesting_fact: Huasheng was the first Jiaxing company to list in 2021. Its IPO was priced at 22.38 yuan and raised 560m yuan for wire-drawing base cloth, advanced composites and an R&D centre.
deep_cut_fact: His drop-stitch ('拉丝气垫') fabric is the core material inside inflatable stand-up paddle boards. The company's product list now also includes BOPP capacitor film.
notes: The only email on the company site is a sales address (emily@huashengflex.com.cn), so it is not listed as a press route. The site has an investor-relations section. Main phone +86-573-87987519. Simply Wall St lists Jiang Yuhui as the largest holder (37.4%) but does not state the relationship.

name: Jan Hruska
current_role: Co-founder of Sophos; Oxford-based angel investor; listed as a director of Virus Bulletin Ltd (aggregator data, not current-verified)
profile: Dr Jan Hruska co-founded the Oxford cybersecurity company Sophos with Peter Lammer in 1985. They started with encryption products and moved into anti-virus software in the late 1980s and 1990s. Apax bought a majority stake in 2010 for $830m. Thoma Bravo acquired Sophos in 2019-20 at an enterprise value of about $3.9bn, and the founders exited before that sale. He is now listed as an angel investor in Oxford.
interesting_fact: He and Lammer met in Oxford in the mid-1980s and started out in a semi-detached house in Kidlington with a grand piano and a German Shepherd. A Norwegian distributor's suggestion pushed them from encryption into anti-virus.
deep_cut_fact: Their first venture was not software but a portable computer, the AC-86. It used a Harris-made 8086-class chip and ran DOS 1. Only one prototype was built and it was never sold.
notes: Low public profile; no personal site or social accounts found. In January 2009 he gave a talk at the Oxford Internet Institute on Sophos's origins (https://www.oii.ox.ac.uk/?p=23198). Sophos history: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sophos. Angel-investor listing: https://nordic9.com/companies/jan-hruska/.
